name: chown
synopsis: int chown(const char *pathname, uid_t owner, gid_t group);
int fchown(int fd, uid_t owner, gid_t group);
int lchown(const char *pathname, uid_t owner, gid_t group);
int fchownat(int dirfd, const char *pathname, uid_t owner, gid_t group, int flags);
description: The chown family of system calls changes the owner and group of a file. They differ in how the file is specified, such as by pathname, file descriptor, or with options for symbolic links. Only privileged processes can change ownership, and certain behaviors depend on the file system and kernel version.

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: Path to the file for chown() and lchown()

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: New owner ID, or -1 to leave unchanged

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: New group ID, or -1 to leave unchanged

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags for fchownat(), such as AT_EMPTY_PATH or AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Search permission is denied on a component of the path prefix
fd is not a valid open file descriptor (for fchown()), or dirfd is invalid (for fchownat())
pathname points outside accessible address space
Invalid flag specified in flags (for fchownat())
A low-level I/O error occurred while modifying the inode (for fchown())
Too many symbolic links were encountered in resolving pathname
A component of the path prefix is not a directory, or dirfd refers to a non-directory (for fchownat())
The calling process did not have the required permissions, or the file is marked immutable
The named file resides on a read-only filesystem

bugs: The behavior for root changing ownership of executable files depends on the kernel version; since Linux 2.2.13, root is treated like other users in clearing S_ISUID and S_ISGID bits.
versions: The 4.4BSD version can be used only by the superuser; feature test macros like _POSIX_C_SOURCE >= 200809L are required for glibc versions.
